# Sovereign Enterprise

> A full AI company on its own devices. Six AI agents (sales, service, finance, operations, systems, audit) run the company end to
> end; two people watch and decide the exceptions; an office hub is the door where the work arrives. Every device is a brain — a
> verified, readable pattern library (the Konomi SLM) that answers only inside what it was verified on and abstains outside it — and
> the brains talk only through signed records on a peer-to-peer spine. Money and security calls need a second, independent brain to
> agree; what no brain can confirm waits for a person. Nothing leaves the building.

Live: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/sovereign-enterprise/
The case for the board: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/sovereign-enterprise/#case

## How the AI company works
- Nine devices: six agents, two people, the office hub. Each has its own Ed25519 key, a grant scoped to its department, and its own
  copy of the company; every write names the writer's previous write (a per-writer hash chain), so a stolen key cannot rewrite the past.
- Work arrives at the hub. An agent answers from its own brain; if it cannot, it posts a signed question and other agents post signed
  replies from their own brains. There is no shared memory: every answer the company acts on is a record every device holds.
- An agent asked about the same work repeatedly adopts the published brain — only if it re-verifies on its own data. A poisoned brain
  is refused by every device that checks it.
- High-stakes calls (holding a payment, credit terms, quarantining a machine) need an independent brain on another device to agree.
- Outcomes come back; an agent regrows its brain and promotes the new one only if it beats the old on outcomes neither saw.
- Inbound text is screened before any brain reads it; a new attack a person confirms becomes a signed antibody every agent re-checks
  on its own genuine messages before adopting it.
- A behaviour watch (Gary W. Floyd's Behavioral Entropy Signatures) pauses an agent that stops behaving like itself — a valid key is
  not enough.
- Free text (reading a customer's message, routing it, drafting a reply) goes to a language model the company chooses — on its own
  machine, in the browser, or a provider with its own key; spend capped before any paid call; every call audited; drafts a person sends.
- Devices on different machines connect directly over WebRTC with no server: a hand-carried code, each key proven on the link.

## Planting it in a business
- One seed, grown into each business's own company. The planter names the kind of business and its headcount and hands over the
  records it already keeps, read on the planter's device and never uploaded: each is classified with the reason; each job gets a brain
  grown from the business's own records (graded on rows it never grew on), the shipped brain, or a person; a decision log is re-grown
  and checked against the old decisions and what really happened.
- Bridges: a bank statement reconciled to the penny, a trial balance as the opening entry, a customer list; out as a Sage Accounting
  journal import and a CRM spreadsheet. Xero is not written (its layout could not be checked against Xero's own documentation).
- The planter's device (the owner's or an admin's — on site, or remote after joining by the invite link) signs the plan into the
  company. Each agent device reads which key really wrote a planted brain, takes it only from the owner, an admin or the agent that runs
  that job, and only if it re-checks on its own records at least as well as the brain it has.
- The signed planting receipt: each job before and after on its own held-out rows, the five-year cost on the business's own headcount,
  the records brought across; a redacted showcase copy (no names, no amounts) for the next prospect.

## Measured (re-runnable: node tools/run-company.mjs --check)
- A working day of 480 pieces of work on published datasets: 78.3% done end to end by agents; 90.7% of agent calls matched the real
  outcome they never saw; 124 money and security calls confirmed by an independent second brain; 30 answered by another device's brain
  over the spine; 104 held for a person; every device converged; books balanced; vault audited. Receipt 5015248ecf411676.
- What those numbers prove (src/evidence.mjs, in the receipt): against doing nothing on the same calls, with an exact test, 3 of
  8 jobs are measurably better (fraud, inventory, intrusion); the rest show no evidence either way yet. The second brain, on
  money and security calls: asked 127 times, agreed 124 (both wrong together 5), disagreed 3, caught 0 of the first
  brain's mistakes — on these datasets the two make the same errors, and the page says so. What it is for, measured in the same re-run:
  with the Finance agent's fraud brain tampered with on its own device, the second brain stopped 7 of 11 wrong money calls
  (0 false alarms); untouched, it caught 0 and raised 3 false alarms.

## The white paper — the AI-native office
- AI runs 90% of a modelled 50-person UK office's operational work on owned machines; five AI-native people oversee it.
- Five-year cost: £12.6m today, £12.7m with an AI seat on every desk, £2.3m AI-native and owned — £10.3m saved (82%).
- Owning the AI capacity vs renting the same dedicated GPUs from AWS London, and how far an AI-native rival can undercut you —
  computed from cited sources on the page.

## Proof
- 384 unit, boundary, hostile-input and integration tests; two byte-reproducible re-runs (the AI company's working day; a
  hostile-network simulation); a mutation + fuzz witness over every decision kernel; a gate on the page's own script.

## The auditor's checker
- https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/sovereign-enterprise/verify.html — drop a signed checkpoint, a proof of one entry or a proof that the books only grew; every signature and hash is checked in your own browser, without trusting the company. Save it as one file and it works offline.
